@humanhorseshoes@mastodon.world The trend is to build complexity that nobody understands, then flail around for software archeologists that can keep the mess running.  

I was responsible for a 1.5 million lines of code. If a customer encountered a problem, I could re-familiarize myself with a few modules then remember where that behavior surfaced, and fix it in a hour or so  I knew how it all worked because I had thought about and built it before later maintaining it. 

#AI code? Somebody knowing it all? Not going to happen. Maybe less money spent upfront on weak skilled low paid staff, but it quickly becomes a black hole. Worse than cloned spaghetti code, it's the average of all previous programmers' code used to train the #LLMs, some seasoned experts some idiots. Never robust, questionable security. Will enrage users with bug after bug, ruining the rep of companies right and left, those that had one left. Glad I retired before #vibecoding became acceptable. I won't be held responsible!

#programming #coding
